intent: Hold the iteration-2 geometry unchanged, as the Integrator requested, so that the kd (0.05 to 0.15) change is the only variable in this race. Keep the five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg and body 0.12 x 0.18 m. I expect max_error to stay near 0.061 m or fall below about 0.058 m, with line loss at zero on every track. I am not considering span, footprint, mass, track, radius or y changes, since none has moved max_error. If the excursion persists, my next geometry proposal needs a named start-up hypothesis and the measurement that would confirm it.
learning: Nine iterations show that geometry has been explored across span, footprint, look-ahead, track, radius and mass. Only span changed line loss, and nothing has moved the 0.061 m excursion. If kd does not change max_error, the excursion is not controlled by any tested geometry or gain, and the next useful evidence is where in the run it occurs. Ask the Integrator to report the step or bend at which max_error peaks on each track (start-up versus a specific bend), and to name the track on which any line_loss_events occur. A start-up transient and a steady offset call for different geometry responses.
rationale:
Nine iterations have now been raced. The best geometry is the iteration-2 row (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.12 x 0.18 m), which scored 26.9949. Iteration 8 (wheel_track 0.10 m) returned the same score and the same max_error (0.0614, 0.0611, 0.0609), so track width is settled. Across all runs, every trial ended off_track with max_error about 0.061 m. That sits just above the fixed off-track limit of max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and the widest allowed body still gives only 0.0575 m, so no body change helps. Levers tested with no effect on max_error: footprint (12 vs 16 mm), wheel_track (0.10, 0.12, 0.15 m), mass (0.6 vs 0.8 kg), wheel_radius (0.03 vs 0.04 m, where 0.04 m scored worse), and sensor y (0.02 and 0.04 m identical; 0.06 m reintroduced line loss). Span of ±0.05 m is the only change that mattered, because it removed line loss.

The Integrator's feedback from iteration 9 is to hold this geometry while they test kd (0.05 to 0.15). They have not yet reported whether that changes the excursion, so there is no new geometry evidence to act on. I take their advice and hold the geometry unchanged. I considered a wider span (±0.07 m) and a seven-sensor row, but neither has a hypothesis that the data supports: span has already removed line loss and has not moved max_error. Proposing either now would be an untested change without a reason.

Expected result: the same score as the best row (about 26.99), zero line loss, and max_error near 0.061 m, unless the kd change moves the controller's response. If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, the Integrator's damping result is real, and I will hold geometry while they tune gains. If it stays at 0.061 m, I will only propose a geometry change backed by a named start-up hypothesis, with the measurement that would confirm it.
